newsitem.title: ESTONIA: PARLIAMENT BOOSTS EXCISE TAX FOR LARGE BREWERS.
newsitem.headline: PARLIAMENT BOOSTS EXCISE TAX FOR LARGE BREWERS.

text.p: Estonia's parliament on Tuesday approved changes to the excise law, which will increase the excise duty for leading brewer Saku and foreign beer importers.
Saku, owned by Baltic Beverages, itself a joint venture between Finnish Hartwall and Nordic brewer Pripps, is the leading beer maker in Estonia.
The law says brewers making over 20 million decalitres of beer, like Saku and foreign firms, must pay three kroons on low alcohol beer and 3.5 kroons on high alcohol beer from July 1.
Under the present law, the excise tax for large producers is 0.50 kroons lower.
Breweries producing 500,000 to 20 million decalitres have a tax rate of 2.5 and 3.00 kroons and for breweries producing 500,000 decalitres, the rate is 2.00 and 2.50 kroons.
Politicians said the state would get about 20 million kroons of additional taxes with the new law.
"The decision was reached as a result of many disputes," a member of the Reform Party fraction, Jurgen Ligi, told Reuters.
"The law will hit Saku and importers and leaves a gap between Estonian producers," he added.
"The law will interfere in the competition between Saku and Tartu Breweries," Ligi said.
Tartu, in which Finnish Olvi bought a 15 percent stake, has been trying to catch more market share from Saku, which is the dominant force on the Estonian market.
"It is in contradiction with the principles of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) and the question is whether we will be forgiven or not," he said.
Estonia has applied for membership of the WTO and hopes to gain it this year.
